unmapped_findings: Fe-6%Al as-cast composition (Table 1): nominal 6 at.% Al; real Al content 6.0 at.% (3.0 wt.-%); impurities C 50 wt.ppm and Si 70 wt.ppm.
The polycrystalline as-cast Fe-6%Al alloy showed a yield stress drop at -100 °C; only Fe-4%Al (the most ductile alloy) and Fe-6%Al produced such low-temperature yield stress drops.

For the as-cast polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys (0-18 at.% Al, which include Fe-6%Al) the room-temperature yield stress increases linearly with Al content; the solid-solution hardening coefficient is about 2.2 GPa, consistent with Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys.
The tensile yield stress equals the compressive yield stress for the studied polycrystalline as-cast alloys at the same rate and temperature.
At -100 °C the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength of the polycrystalline as-cast alloys are higher than those at room temperature by about 80 MPa.
